capabilities: Read the full note aloud with a neural TTS voice
Summarize the note with an LLM and read the summary
Control playback with pause, resume, stop, loop, and auto-next
Convert Markdown elements like tables, code blocks, and links into speech-friendly text
disambiguation: Not an audio recorder; it converts note text to spoken audio rather than capturing recordings.
extras: Desktop-only plugin; speech synthesis itself needs no API key, only the optional LLM summarization does. Documentation is bilingual (English/Chinese).
motivation: The author built it for people who learn better by listening or want to rest their eyes after writing, turning the vault into a personal podcast.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to listen to notes; reading long notes requires keeping your eyes on the screen.

relations.evidence: TTS is powered by Microsoft Edge TTS (msedge-tts) — no API key or additional setup required
Works with any OpenAI-compatible API — OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (通义), Zhipu (智谱), and more

requires.name: LLM API key for OpenAI-compatible summarization service

summary: Text-to-speech plugin that reads notes aloud via Microsoft Edge TTS, with optional LLM-summarized readings and playlist-style playback controls.
